_meta.status: Built 2026-07-22 from 17 e-reader screenshots of Colavita's memoir, ch. 9 ('Chicken Valley'). Second full-chapter digest for this source (first: 08-angry-skipper). Unlike ch. 8, this chapter overlaps substantially with material Michael had already excerpted directly into events/operation-sheridan-sabre-1968-12-04 and its verbal-account document (colavita-henry-verbal-account-dec4-1968) BEFORE this digest pipeline existed -- the verbatim quotes on that document are word-for-word matches to this chapter's p3 and p5. The full-chapter read still surfaces a large amount of new material beyond those two excerpted paragraphs: the night mortar/ground assault's full color (chaplain, Lt. Johnson's foxhole incident, the 'GOOKS IN THE WIRE' call, the Blue Max pilot's radio plea), the entirely new 21 Jan 1969 death of SP4 Elliot Velez-Rodriguez (already on the KIA list but with no event page or account until now), a second independent primary-source account of the 28 Jan 1969 bunker-complex fight (previously sourced only from a 2016 oral history video), the Christmas personnel swap (Johnson out, Babas in), the Claymore 'clapper keyboard' invention, and a postwar visit to Tangier Island that resolves the source of the existing Eskridge gravesite photo and surfaces a documentation error in a condolence letter ghostwritten by Lt. Derums.
_meta.notes: Narrator is CPT Henry 'Rocky' Colavita (soldiers/colavita-henry) -- as in ch. 8, not named by his real name anywhere in this chapter's text (referred to as 'Skipper' by Lt. Johnson; self-identifies only via reflection on his own command). Identity confirmed by cross-reference to the existing colavita-henry profile, not from this chapter alone.
_meta.copyright_note: Source is a copyrighted, commercially published memoir (Hellgate Press, 2015). This digest extracts FACTS ONLY (names, ranks, units, dates, locations, event summaries) in paraphrase. No sentence-level quoting beyond short phrases already published elsewhere on the archive (e.g. the 'worst day in my life' passage, already quoted in full on colavita-henry-verbal-account-dec4-1968 from this same chapter). Do not expand this file with new verbatim passages -- if a specific phrase needs preserving, flag it in the review.md for a judgment call, per the standing rule set in Session 101 and the Excerpt/visible-link convention set 2026-07-22 (see sources/colavita/index.md).

Internally dated events: 4 Dec 1968 (ambush + night assault) -> 5 Dec (Arclight, withdrawal) -> 6 Dec (skipped ambush) -> 7 Dec ('Pearl Harbor Day', resume ops) -> Christmas period (~Dec 1968, undated) -> 21 Jan 1969 (Velez-Rodriguez) -> 28 Jan 1969 (Pipher/Eskridge bunker fight) -> postwar (undated).

(2) 'p6' is simply absent from the folder -- no gap in narrative content is apparent across the p5->p7 boundary (the Cromie/R&R anecdote wraps up, a scene-break '****' follows, then a new reflective passage opens 'As I believe I said earlier...'), and the %-counter only advances by 1 minute across that boundary (consistent with adjacent pages, not a skipped one) -- so this is treated as a missing/unnecessary filename, not a content gap, but flagged since it cannot be verified with full certainty. 'photos.jpg' is NOT placed in the narrative sequence above: its own %-counter (52%, 16 min left) would put it between p3 and p4, but its content -- a group photo captioned '...Bob Babas (Rifle Range 6), Dave Spingath (Wild Cat 6), and Preston Karr (White Skull 6)' -- depicts a platoon-leader roster that could not exist until AFTER Babas replaces Johnson (Christmas ~late Dec 1968, per p13) and, per Karr's own existing soldier profile (soldiers/karr-john), Karr did not arrive in-country until 1969-03-12 -- a full five weeks after this chapter's own last narrated date (28 Jan 1969). This means the photo page is either a later-chapter photo insert that landed in this folder's capture batch by mistake, or (more likely, matching the print-book convention already seen in ch. 8's front-matter photo) a photo-section page whose position in the e-book does not track the surrounding chapter's narrated timeline. personnel.name: Lieutenant Douglas "Doug" Magruder
personnel.slug_candidate: none yet -- stub candidate (unchanged from ch. 8; see site/_docs/stub-candidates.md)

personnel.name: Lieutenant Michael Johnson
personnel.slug_candidate: none yet -- stub candidate (unchanged from ch. 8; see site/_docs/stub-candidates.md)
personnel.role: Platoon leader, Rifle Range (3rd Plt) -- through Christmas ~Dec 1968, then reassigned to battalion staff
personnel.note: MAJOR new material. During the Dec 4-5 night mortar attack, found already lying at the bottom of the CP foxhole when Colavita and four others jump in -- claims he was 'checking the perimeter' when the mortars started. Colavita publicly needles him ('Rifle Range is better off without you tonight') and privately debates whether this was cowardice; consults SFC Adams and the Rifle Range NCOs, who report Johnson 'showed no initiative, no leadership ability and inspired no one' but stop short of confirming cowardice. Colavita decides not to send him back on a chopper immediately (to avoid humiliating him) but privately plans to leave him on Rita next rotation. At Christmas, Colonel Henry takes Johnson off Colavita's hands in exchange for a newly arrived 2LT (Bob Babas) -- Johnson is 'screwed... into a hole somewhere on the battalion staff.' This resolves/closes out the ch. 8 'suspicions'/RTO-walking thread with a concrete outcome: Johnson left the company for good at Christmas 1968.

personnel.name: Sergeant Terry Shoopman
personnel.note: Wild Cat squad leader who, short of men for LZ perimeter defense on the night of 20-21 Jan 1969, used his own initiative to insert newly arrived replacement Elliot Velez-Rodriguez into the line rather than have him wait for an Alpha Company chopper. The next morning, while checking the perimeter after an unexplained explosion, Shoopman was the one who found Velez-Rodriguez's remains (having personally placed him there the night before).

personnel.name: SP4 Elliot Velez-Rodriguez
personnel.cross_ref: ALREADY on the KIA list (site/_docs/d-co-kia-list.md, 1969-01-21, `[att]`, no profile yet) but has NO event page and NO account anywhere on the archive until this chapter. Highest-priority stub/event candidate this chapter surfaces.
personnel.role: Replacement soldier, inbound to A Company, 2/8 Cav -- inserted into D Co's (Wild Cat's) LZ Rita perimeter defense for one night only
personnel.note: Arrived on LZ Rita while Alpha Company was in the field and Delta was on LZ defense; Sgt. Shoopman inserted him into Wild Cat's perimeter line for the night rather than have him sit out unassigned. A single explosion in the middle of Rita that night sympathetically set off stacked mortar rounds in the ammo pit; no attack followed, and a morning headcount found all Delta troopers present -- but a severed arm was then found near the ammo storage pit, leading to the discovery of Velez-Rodriguez's remains (his 'remains were scooped up and poured into a body bag' rather than placed). Cause disputed even in the book: theories include self-inflicted (accident or suicide) versus an enemy satchel charge slung onto the LZ from a bent-over tree 'like a slingshot' (patrols later found evidence of enemy activity just outside the wire, supporting this theory). Official Army cause of death: 'Artillery, rocket or mortar' -- consistent with the KIA list's current 'Hostile' classification, though the book itself never resolves which specific cause. Colavita initially reasoned Velez-Rodriguez 'wasn't officially in my company' and shouldn't count in Delta's body count, then explicitly rejects that reasoning: 'he died serving with D Company, doing a D Company job... he absolutely does count... included on the Honor Roll with the other KIA members of Delta Company.' Panel 34W, Line 54 (matches the KIA list exactly).

personnel.note: Named directly by the memoir for the first time (previously this event's only firsthand account was a 2016 oral history video that never named him) -- 'Carl Pipher from Canton, Ohio... twenty years old... personnel.name: CPL Warren Reed Eskridge
personnel.note: Named directly by the memoir for the first time (see Pipher note above) -- 'Warren Eskridge from Tangier, Virginia... twenty-one years old... Panel 33 West, Line 7.' The gravesite photo already appearing on p4 (with the Dec 4 KIA table, an anachronistic placement -- see events below) is confirmed by p17 to have been taken during a POSTWAR visit Colavita made to Tangier Island, VA with two other 'Angry Skipper' veterans (Ed Regan and Mike McGhie -- see personnel/events below), where they met Eskridge's family (including his twin brother, at the time the island's mayor) and laid the wreath visible in the photo. During that visit, Eskridge's sister produced a condolence letter attributed to Colavita's signature block but actually ghostwritten by Lt. Karl Derums (the company XO's known duty, per ch. 8's digest) -- Colavita disputes a factual claim in the letter that Eskridge 'walked into an ambush,' insisting Delta never did (they were either ambushed or the ones ambushing). See soldiers/derums-karl for the enrichment.

personnel.name: Lieutenant Karl Derums
personnel.note: Two new enrichment items. (1) Fabricated three Claymore 'clapper keyboard' devices (a plywood board holding six clappers, so an ambush team could fire six mines in sequence with one operator) from a field sketch Delta sent him in the rear, then sent them back out on resupply -- confirms and extends ch. 8's existing note that Derums 'formalizes award recommendations' and handles rear-echelon admin duties, adding a hands-on fabrication/logistics task. (2) During the postwar Tangier Island visit, Colavita learns Derums ghostwrote the condolence letter to Eskridge's family over Colavita's own unsigned signature block (standard XO duty per ch. 8's digest -- 'writes letters to families of KIA/WIA') -- but the letter contained a factual claim ('walked into an ambush') Colavita specifically disputes as untrue to how Delta operated. Colavita's own reaction ('I wished that Karl had been in the same room, so I could kill him') is strong language but clearly rhetorical/retrospective, not a real incident.

locations.name: LZ Rita
locations.detail: Continues as D Co's base through the Christmas period and the 21 Jan 1969 Velez-Rodriguez incident. New detail this chapter: rats 'the size of house cats' infested the bunkers due to cookie-crumb residue from Christmas care packages; a Signal Corps field-expedient patch let soldiers make brief phone calls home (Colavita spoke to his mother) using a military radio net protocol (saying 'over').
locations.cross_ref: Already a full location page at locations/fsb-rita (grid XT505795). No date/occupancy change -- these are color/atmosphere details for an already-established occupancy window (2/8 Cav held Rita through the 30 Jan 1969 relief by 2/5 Cav, matching the existing event-page timeline).

locations.name: Fire Support Base Saint Barbara
locations.type: fire support base, not organic to 1st Cavalry Division
locations.detail: The base D Co (and the rest of 2/8 Cav) moved to after abandoning LZ Rita, per Colonel Henry's advance briefing. Former French fort; sits in the 25th Infantry Division's ('Tropic Lightning') AO, so 2/8 Cav did NOT provide its own perimeter security there (25th ID troops did) -- freeing all four of Henry's line companies for simultaneous search-and-destroy. Hosted Corps-level artillery: in addition to the usual 105mm/155mm, Saint Barbara had 175mm pieces and 8-inch guns, supporting RVN/ROK/allied units in range too. Named for Saint Barbara, patron saint of artillery (explicitly NOT named for a commander's wife, per the author's aside). Located close to Nui Ba Den (see next entry).
locations.cross_ref: Matches the 'FB Saint Barbara' candidate already flagged (unconfirmed, coordinates TBD) in soldiers/colavita-henry.md's admin notes, which explicitly warned against conflating it with a false-match 199th LIB/25th Arty coordinate near Xuan Loc. This chapter's detail (25th ID AO, former French fort, Corps-level artillery, near Nui Ba Den) is the richest description of the site the archive has yet -- worth a real push on the gazetteer/fsb-locations research now that a location (near Nui Ba Den / Tay Ninh Province, NOT Xuan Loc) is implied. Nui Ba Den itself is a well-known, well-gazetteered landmark (Tay Ninh Province), so Saint Barbara's location can likely be narrowed considerably from this alone.
locations.confidence: medium -- narrative detail is high-confidence (author's own description), but no grid is given and the site is not yet independently confirmed against a period map/ORLL

locations.name: Nui Ba Den ("Black Virgin Mountain" / "Black Lady Mountain")
locations.detail: 3,268 ft peak, the only elevation on otherwise flat terrain near FSB Saint Barbara; Americans held the summit, VC/NVA reportedly held everything else including tunnel-honeycombed interior passages. Author disputes the common US-soldier translation 'Black Virgin Mountain,' preferring 'Black Lady Mountain' per his own Vietnamese-language training (referencing an in-book cross-link to 'Chapter Five' for the underlying language lesson -- confirms the book itself has internal chapter cross-references).
locations.cross_ref: Well-known, independently gazetteered landmark in Tay Ninh Province -- useful primarily as a locating aid for Saint Barbara (see above), not itself a new archive location requiring research.

locations.name: Tangier Island, Virginia (and Crisfield, Maryland)
locations.detail: Home of CPL Warren Eskridge; Colavita and two other 'Angry Skipper' veterans (Ed Regan, Mike McGhie) visited postwar, hitching a mail/supply boat ride from Crisfield, MD, to lay a wreath at Eskridge's grave and meet his family (his twin brother, then the island's mayor). Parallel to ch. 8's Fort Benning reunion -- another postwar site tied to this memoir's veterans.
locations.cross_ref: New postwar location, not part of the wartime gazetteer -- relevant only as context for the Eskridge profile enrichment (see personnel above), not a candidate for the FSB/location gazetteer.

events.notes: Approach march under Colonel Henry's Charlie-Charlie guidance; company sees/hears Spooky (AC-130 gunship), Blue Max Cobras, armed Hueys/Loaches working the fight ahead; a disabled Cobra passes low overhead and crashes nearby (aviation battalion scrambles a recovery); men see chickens scatter, naming the area on the spot. Already summarized on the existing event page/document -- this is the fuller version of the same story, no new facts, just richer color (the Spooky/Cobra visual detail is new relative to the terse existing summary).

events.notes: Battalion chaplain (unnamed) present in Colavita's CP, joins the CP foxhole when the mortars start; Lt. Johnson found already at the bottom of the same foxhole (see personnel note); Cat 6 (Spingath) reports the enemy trying to turn Wild Cat's Claymores; Magruder reports enemy penetration of White Skull's wire; Colavita makes the 'GOOKS IN THE WIRE' call on both company and battalion nets, sharply increasing outgoing fire; a Blue Max Cobra pilot is heard on the battalion net requesting permission to break formation over 'hundreds of gooks in the open,' granted. Fight lasts most of the night; perimeter holds with only slight, quickly-repaired rupture. No KIA to either company -- matches existing summary exactly.

events.location: Chicken Valley cache site -> unspecified march destination
events.cross_ref: Matches the existing event page's Arclight/COSVN paragraph exactly (site ultimately assessed as NOT the elusive COSVN HQ; B-52 Arclight struck the position after C&D withdrew to a safe distance). No new facts about the strike decision itself.
events.notes: New color: resupply/medevac handled quickly via the secure interior LZ; VIPs (brigade/division staff, intel officers) lifted out before dark, leaving C&D to handle the expected counterattack alone (framed by the author as appropriate); daylight revealed grisly claymore-turner casualties at the wire ('Sin Loi'); companies walked out (not lifted) to separate grid coordinates from Stone Mountain 6, 'just get the hell out from under the Arclight' -- no assigned objective. Companies felt the actual B-52 strike as ground tremors even after clearing to a 'danger close' distance.

Minor, candid admission: exhausted from two sleepless nights, Colavita 'forgot' to plan an ambush for the night of 6 Dec and instead picked easy defensible terrain and stood the company down early, reasoning they were moving away from both the fight's ground zero and the nearby Cambodian border (implying the company's general operating area was near the border). Not event-page-worthy; a footnote-level personnel/command-style detail.
'Pearl Harbor Day' -- company resumes search-and-destroy patrolling. Purely a calendar marker; no incident described.

As Christmas approached, Colonel Henry rotated all four 2/8 Cav companies through LZ Rita so each got goodie boxes from home and an Army Christmas meal; division sent the division band around to firebases; a Signal Corps field-expedient patch let soldiers make brief phone calls home over a military radio net (Colavita called his mother; both parties had to say 'over'). Colonel Henry's best Christmas gift to Colavita: taking Lt. Johnson off his hands in exchange for newly arrived 2LT Bob Babas, who takes over Rifle Range platoon for the rest of Colavita's command (paralleling Spingath at Wild Cat, per the author's own comparison). This is the personnel-change event that resolves the ch. 8 Johnson thread -- worth folding into a Johnson stub-candidate note and a new Babas stub if/when built.

Company devises a 'clapper keyboard' -- a half-inch plywood board holding six Claymore clackers in individual quarter-inch-walled slots, letting one ambush operator fire six mines in rapid sequence ('looks somewhat like he's playing the piano'). Sketch sent to Lt. Derums in the rear, who has three fabricated and sent back out on resupply. Minor, colorful, not event-page-worthy -- a good detail for Derums's enrichment and possibly a 'material culture' footnote on colavita-henry's ambush-doctrine narrative.

events.location: LZ Rita, near an ammo storage pit under steel planking
units: D Co, 2/8 Cav -- Wild Cat (2nd Plt)
events.cross_ref: ENTIRELY NEW EVENT -- SP4 Elliot Velez-Rodriguez is already on site/_docs/d-co-kia-list.md (1969-01-21, `[att]`, profile status '--') but has NO event page and NO prior account anywhere on the archive. This is the strongest single new-event candidate this chapter produces.
events.notes: A single explosion in the middle of LZ Rita on the night of 20-21 Jan 1969 sympathetically set off stacked mortar rounds in the ammo pit; no ground attack followed. Morning headcount found all Delta troopers present, but a severed arm was found near the ammo storage pit during a perimeter check, leading to the discovery of the remains of Velez-Rodriguez -- a replacement bound for A Company whom Sgt. Shoopman had inserted into Wild Cat's LZ defense line for that one night, being short-handed. Cause disputed in the text itself: self-inflicted (accidental or intentional) vs. an enemy satchel charge slung onto the LZ via a bent-over tree, 'like a slingshot' (patrols later found signs of enemy activity just outside the wire, supporting this theory). Official Army-assigned cause: 'Artillery, rocket or mortar' (consistent with the KIA list's current 'Hostile' tag). Colavita explicitly includes him on Delta's own Honor Roll despite his attached/transient status -- consistent with the KIA list's `[att]` inclusion-reason marking already applied. RECOMMEND: a new event page (events/operation-sheridan-sabre-1969-01-21) and, per the 'ask before creating' rule, a stub-decision for Velez-Rodriguez's own profile -- Michael's call, but this is a real KIA with a real, if disputed, cause narrative, not just a bare casualty-record line anymore.

events.location: unmapped enemy base camp, D Co AO near LZ Rita
events.cross_ref: Matches events/operation-sheridan-sabre-1969-01-28 and colavita-henry-verbal-account-jan28-1969 in circumstance and outcome, but this is a SECOND, INDEPENDENT primary source for the same event -- the existing account was transcribed from a 2016 oral history video and never named either casualty; this memoir passage names both men directly for the first time and adds detail the oral history didn't (three-platoon-front approach, orange strobe lights vs. flares, the explicit contrast to Chicken Valley's flare use).
events.notes: On 28 Jan 1969, Delta walked into a prepared enemy base camp on a three-platoon front, took immediate heavy fire and casualties; Colavita ordered platoons to disengage and get behind cover, called for gunship support, and advised Stone Mountain 6. The enemy stayed in prepared bunkers/foxholes rather than press the attack, giving the gunships room to work. Fight continued into and through the night; company used orange strobe lights (not parachute flares, since they were dug in above ground rather than in foxholes as at Chicken Valley -- flares would have exposed them). NVA probed the perimeter repeatedly but never broke in. Two KIA: Warren Eskridge (Tangier, VA, Panel 33W/Line 7) and Carl Pipher (Canton, OH, Panel 33W/Line 11) -- matches the existing event page/profiles exactly.

Colavita and two fellow veterans (Ed Regan, Mike McGhie) visited Tangier Island postwar to lay a wreath at CPL Eskridge's grave and meet his family, including his twin brother (then the island's mayor). During the visit, Eskridge's sister showed Colavita a condolence letter, ostensibly from him, that he had never actually written or signed -- ghostwritten by Lt. Karl Derums (the company XO, per his known letter-writing duty) over Colavita's unsigned signature block. The letter claimed Eskridge 'walked into an ambush,' a characterization Colavita disputes as factually wrong for how Delta operated. This is the source of the gravesite photo that appears (out of chronological place) on p4 alongside the Dec 4, 1968 KIA table -- not a new wartime event, but directly relevant to the Eskridge profile and a good example of a documentation-accuracy issue worth noting if this letter is ever independently located.
